boundary_violations: ProductCatalog implicitly depends on ProductContext (for Product entity to search, browse, and view detailed information about products as per REQ-015, REQ-016, REQ-020, REQ-021) but ProductContext is not in its allowed_dependencies.

ProductContext implicitly depends on UserAuthentication (for User details related to Offer, Request, and Product ownership/interaction as per REQ-048, REQ-050, REQ-049) but UserAuthentication is not in its allowed_dependencies.
ProductManagement implicitly depends on ProductContext (to add product as per REQ-022, implying creation of a Product instance) but ProductContext is not in its allowed_dependencies.
ownership_conflicts: ContactNumber is defined as both an Entity and a Value Object within the UserAuthentication context.
Email is defined as both an Entity and a Value Object within the UserAuthentication context.
PricingDetail is defined as both an Entity and a Value Object within the ProductManagement context.
Redundant Value Objects in UserAuthentication: UserEmail and Email both represent email; UserName and Name both represent name.
SellerDetail is defined as both an Entity and a Value Object within the ProductCatalog context.

Semantic overlap: PricingDetail (VO in ProductManagement) and ProductPrice (VO in ProductContext) both represent the price of a product, leading to ambiguity in ownership and representation of a core product attribute.
semantic_drift: The model separates Product (in ProductContext) and ProductDetail (in ProductManagement) without explicitly defining their relationship, which drifts from the requirement that 'product details' (REQ-016, REQ-021, REQ-051) are inherently part of a Product (REQ-049). This implies a loss of the semantic rule that product details belong to a product.
